reviews.title: Accessibility
reviews.text: Since the last iOS update the app is longer accessible to the visually impaired. Unless it’s sorted in the next update I will be cancelling my subscription. I would also encourage other visually impaired people to do the same.

reviews.title: Add option to remove calorie goal
reviews.text: I downloaded this app to keep track of my macros (especially protein). My weight is very consistent, so I don’t need any help limiting my calories. Some days I eat less than maintenance, other days I eat more. That makes it pretty annoying when I eat more than my budget (usually trying to reach my protein goal or balancing out a below-maintenance day earlier in the week) and the apple widget goes red. Can we have an option to turn it off  and focus only on the numbers?

reviews.text: I paid for a month just to make it stop with the interruptions. It only got rid of the subscription begging but still wants to spam you with demands you enable permissions and use features. I know how I want to use it, leave me alone. Won't resubscribe.

reviews.title: Tries to do way too much and fails as a result
reviews.text:
All I really want is something to help me track my eating habits and evaluate them. The only reason why I'm not just using a notepad is because it can be a pain to the research myself. Unfortunately, half the time it feels like I have to do that anyways with this app. Some foods are listed too many times, making you have to figure out which is the one you're looking for, and some aren't listed at all, so you either have to find the closest equivalent or input it manually. The homepage is a mess even with the ability to "customize" it, which isn't too much of a surprise given how you can't rearrange or get rid of certain meal slots without a premium subscription. Something it tends to push on you alongside a hundred other "helpful tips" even when you turn them off. The search function doesn't always prioritize your recipes, meaning you have to go digging for the day and meal you last entered it in for. This is all without getting into their "premium AI scanning" that failed for me on the one freebie they gave out. 

But hey, you can technically use it to log food so 2 stars.

reviews.title: If you actually cook - don’t waste your time.
reviews.text: This app is absolutely useless if you actually make your own meals. The ai scan your meal feature is woefully inaccurate. I scanned my breakfast, which it read as chia pudding coming in at 157 calories. I then had to manually search for the ingredients I had used, and once I’d found, inputted weights and saved them it came in at 589 calories. A huge difference if you are actually trying to lose weight and are relying on this feature. I can’t barcode scan the majority of the ingredients I use to make a meal as they don’t come in packets, so this app rather defeats the object for me. I can manually enter ingredients into other apps for free if I want, so would use them if I were looking at counting calories.  If most of your food/meals come prepared or from a packet then this may be the app for you, sadly it isn’t for me.

reviews.title: Meals/recipes
reviews.text:
When creating meals or recipes, it would be really helpful to have the option to enter the total cooked weight of the finished meal. The app could then calculate the calories based on the weight of each portion, instead of treating the entire recipe as a single serving.

This used to be a feature, but it seems to have been removed for some reason. It was much more accurate and convenient, so I’d love to see it brought back.

reviews.title: AI Coach is dangerous
reviews.text:
AI Coach is dangerous and very unhealthy. One week I lost 4lbs and it LOWERED my calories from 1300 to 1078! This week I’ve lost 1lb and said my calorie intake would have to be 748 to lose weight and it turned itself off. If someone is not in tune or common sense to actually eat more, this is extremely dangerous. It also tells me “you’ve been fasting, it’s missing food entries, please log your food now. I’ve opened a ticket a week ago with no response. 

Response on your answer: my goal was only set to 1.5 lbs a week, I kept losing weight and AI kept lowering my calorie budget even more every check-in. I’d already declined going from 1300 to 1078 because that was already way too little calories. Then I lost 1lb more the next week (by eating more calories actually around 1400 or so) and AI said I’d need to lower my budget to only 748 calories!! I didn’t set an unrealistic goal, your AI tool  gave dangerously low calories when I was eating double the calories and losing 1lb a week. 

Stop making excuses about my settings or expectations being wrong and look into your own tool. AI is dangerously inaccurate. I stopped using the app completely because of this.

reviews.title: Wrong calories - terrible connection to Garmin
reviews.text: This app has some great features that I love, however it’s calorie burn formula is way off. I’ve had to put the settings down to “sedentary” (I actually run 10-15km per week, and do at least 13k steps a day) and cut my height by 20cm just to get it closer to the actual amount of calories I burn in day, otherwise it tells me I burnt about 300 calories more than what my Apple Watch activity app. I only recently discovered this difference when I put on 2 kg and could not figure out why. In summary, it’s a really bad calorie formula, so be prepared to change settings to get it closer to reality. In addition, it connected well with my previous Apple Watch but has a poor connection to Garmin watches. Over 12,000 steps today so far, and it’s still stuck on 0 steps. I’m not impressed.
